# Magic reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-magic-docs.js — edit the docs in src/magics/ instead. -->

Line magics start a line with `%`; cell magics start a cell with `%%` and take the rest of the cell as input.
Magic lines can also be mixed into JavaScript cells. `%help name` shows the same text inside cinder.

## General

### `%help [name]`

Keys, syntax and every magic; %help name explains one magic. Also: `%quickref`.

### `%config [name[=value]]`

Show or change settings for this session: %config, %config name, %config name=value. Save them in config.json to keep them.

### `%theme [name]`

Switch the color theme (void, nebula, matrix); without an argument, list them.

### `%xmode [minimal|plain|context|verbose]`

How errors are shown: minimal (one line), plain (the standard stack), context (your code around each frame, the default) or verbose (every frame, causes and extra fields).

### `%editmode [vi|emacs]`

Key bindings for the input: %editmode vi or %editmode emacs (%vi switches to vi). Without an argument, show the current one. Also: `%vi`.

### `%layout [block|box]`

Switch the prompt layout: block (full-width input bar) or box (rounded box, like ember's classic look).

### `%depth [n]`

How many levels deep results are printed (default 4; Infinity for everything).

### `%clear`

Clear the screen (also Ctrl+L). Also: `%cls`.

### `%exit [code]`

Leave cinder (also Ctrl+D, exit or .exit). Also: `%quit`.

### `%lsmagic`

List every line and cell magic.

### `%precision [digits]`

Digits after the decimal point for printed numbers: %precision 3. Alone, back to how JavaScript prints them. Only the display changes, not the values.

### `%automagic [on|off]`

Run magics without the % prefix (cd .., pwd, ls): %automagic on/off, or alone to toggle.

### `%page [expr]`

Show a value in full (every level, every item) in your pager ($PAGER, or less). Default: the last result.

## Namespace & inspection

### `%who`

List the variables you defined in this session.

### `%whos`

Your variables as a table: name, type and value.

### `%reset [-f]`

Delete your variables and the result history (_, _N, Out). Asks you to confirm with -f.

### `%del name…`

Delete a variable, including references to it in Out and _N. Also: `%xdel`.

### `%pinfo [-s] expr`

Inspect an object, like obj? (add -s for the source, like obj??). Also: `%inspect`.

### `%psearch pattern`

Search names with wildcards, like Math.*round*? — e.g. %psearch *Array*.

### `%who_ls`

Your variable names, returned as a sorted array.

### `%reset_selective [-f] regex`

Delete the variables whose names match a regular expression (confirm with -f).

### `%pdef expr`

The signature of a function or class.

### `%pdoc expr`

The JSDoc comment of a function defined in one of your cells.

### `%psource expr`

The source of a function or class, highlighted.

### `%pfile expr`

Where a function or class was defined, and the file around it (cells show as cell N).

## Running & timing

### `%time code`

Time one statement or expression: wall and CPU time. The value is returned.

### `%timeit [-n N] [-r R] [-q] [-o] code`

Time a statement, choosing the number of loops automatically. -n loops, -r runs (default 7), -q quiet, -o return a TimeitResult (.average, .stdev, .best, .all_runs). Async code is awaited on each loop.

### `%run [-t] file [args…]`

Run a .js/.mjs/.cjs or .ts/.mts/.cts file in this session (TypeScript is compiled, enums and all): its top-level variables and functions become yours. `require`, `import`, `import.meta`, __dirname and process.argv point at the file; process.exit() only ends the file. -t prints how long it took.

### `%load [-r lines] file`

Put a file (or lines of it: -r 5-10) into the input, to edit before running.

### `%edit [-x] [file]`

Open a file (or, with no file, the previous cell) in $EDITOR, then run it when you close the editor. -x edits without running. Also: `%ed`.

### `%debugger [-w] [port | off]`

Open the V8 inspector so Chrome DevTools (chrome://inspect) or VS Code can attach; `debugger;` statements then pause there. -w waits until a debugger attaches; `%debugger off` closes it. Also: `%inspector`.

### `%profile [-l N] code`

Profile a statement with the V8 CPU profiler and show where the time went (self time per function). -l N shows N rows. Also: `%prun`.

### `%tb [minimal|plain|context|verbose]`

Show the last error again, optionally in another %xmode: %tb verbose.

### `%paste [-q]`

Run the code on the clipboard (prompts like > are removed). -q runs it without showing it.

### `%cpaste [-q]`

Paste or type a block of code, then end it with a line holding only -- (or Ctrl+D); it runs as one cell. Prompts like > are removed.

### `%autoreload [0|1|2]`

Reload CommonJS files you changed before each cell, updating the objects you already hold (exports objects and class methods): %autoreload 2 for every file you required, 1 for only the %aimport-ed ones, 0 to stop. Alone, reloads changed files now. ES modules are cached by Node and can't be reloaded.

### `%aimport [module…]`

Mark a file for %autoreload 1 (and require it): %aimport ./lib.js. Alone, lists the marked files.

### `%%time`

Time the whole cell.

### `%%timeit [-n N] [-r R] [-q] [-o] [setup]`

Time the whole cell; code on the %%timeit line runs once first, as setup. Same options as %timeit.

### `%%profile [-l N]`

Profile the whole cell. -l N shows N rows. Also: `%%prun`.

### `%%capture [--no-stdout] [--no-stderr] [--no-display] [name]`

Run the cell and keep its output instead of printing it: %%capture out, then out.stdout, out.stderr, out.outputs, or out() to show it. --no-stdout, --no-stderr and --no-display let those through.

## History & session

### `%history [-n] [-o] [-p] [-u] [-g pattern] [-l N] [-f file] [range…]`

Show input history. Ranges: 4, 4-6, 4:6 (end exclusive), ~1/ (the whole previous session), ~2/3-5. -n line numbers, -o outputs, -g pattern searches every session (glob), -l N the last N lines, -u unique, -f file writes to a file, -p adds > prompts. Also: `%hist`.

### `%recall [range]`

Put history lines back into the input for editing (default: the previous line). Also: `%rep`.

### `%rerun [-l N] [range]`

Run history lines again as one cell (default: the previous line). -l N reruns the last N lines.

### `%save [-a] [-f] file [range]`

Save history lines to a file (default: every line of this session). -a appends; -f overwrites without asking.

### `%macro name range`

Name a range of history: %macro setup 1-4, then typing `setup` alone runs those lines again. The macro is a variable, so it can be %store-d.

### `%store [-r] [-d name] [-z] [name…]`

Keep variables across sessions: %store name… saves them, -r [name…] restores, -d name deletes, -z deletes all, alone lists them. Values are saved with the structured clone algorithm (objects, arrays, Map, Set, Date, typed arrays…); functions are saved as source.

### `%logstart [-o] [-t] [file]`

Log every cell you run to a file (default cinder_log.js, appended). -o also logs results as comments, -t adds timestamps. %logoff / %logon pause and resume, %logstate shows it, %logstop ends it.

### `%logoff`

Pause logging.

### `%logon`

Resume logging.

### `%logstate`

Show where and how cells are logged.

### `%logstop`

Stop logging.

## Shell & files

### `%cd [dir | - | -N | -b bookmark]`

Change directory: ~ by default, - for the previous one, -N for entry N of %dhist, -b name or a bookmark name. require() and import follow.

### `%pwd`

The current directory (returned as a string).

### `%bookmark [-l] [-d name] [name [dir]]`

Bookmark a directory (the current one by default) for %cd -b name. -l lists them, -d name deletes one.

### `%env [NAME[=value]]`

Environment variables: %env lists them, %env NAME shows one, %env NAME=value sets it.

### `%sx command`

Run a shell command and return its output as an array of lines. $name and ${expr} insert JS values. Also: `%system`.

### `%alias [name command]`

Define a shell alias used as %name: %s is replaced by an argument, %l by the rest of the line. %alias alone lists them.

### `%unalias name`

Remove an alias.

### `%npm args…`

Run npm in the current directory, e.g. %npm install lodash — then require() or import it right away.

### `%pushd [dir]`

Change directory, remembering the current one on a stack for %popd.

### `%popd`

Go back to the directory on top of the %pushd stack.

### `%dirs`

The directory stack (returned as an array, current directory first).

### `%dhist [n]`

Directories you visited this session; %cd -N goes back to entry N. -n limits to the last n.

### `%copy [expr]`

Copy a value to the clipboard (default: the last result). Strings are copied as they are, other values as JSON when possible, else as printed.

### `%killbgscripts`

Stop every background job started with --bg.

### `%%bash [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with bash. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%sh [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with sh. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%zsh [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with zsh. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%python [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with python3. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%python3 [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with python3. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%ruby [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with ruby. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%perl [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with perl. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%node [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with a separate node process (as an ES module). -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%deno [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with deno. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%bun [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] [args…]`

Run the cell with bun. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%script [-o var] [--err var] [--bg] program [args…]`

Run the cell with any program, e.g. %%script ruby -w. -o/--out var and --err var capture its output; --bg runs it in the background.

### `%%writefile [-a] path`

Write the cell to a file (-a appends). Also: `%%file`.
